title: Effective Climate Action Requires Capable States
gist: Subscriber-exclusive teaser: Mariana Mazzucato argues that as COP31 convenes in Antalya, Turkey, the real question is not whether governments should do more on climate but whether they have the state capabilities to do so, which many lack after 40 years of free-market orthodoxy.

themes.theme: State capacity as the climate-implementation bottleneck

insights.claim: The key climate question is no longer whether governments should do more but whether they have the capabilities to do so, and after 40 years of free-market orthodoxy many simply do not.
insights.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato
insights.so_what: Climate-policy delivery risk lies in state execution capacity, not just ambition; implementation lags may persist.
insights.quote: After 40 years of free-market orthodoxy, many simply do not.

insights.claim: At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, themed 'Driving Implementation through Cooperation and Collective Action,' delegates face the familiar challenge of turning long-standing climate commitments into tangible results.
insights.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato
insights.so_what: Watch COP31 for implementation mechanisms rather than new pledges.
insights.locator: LONDON—The United Nations Climate Change Conference
